events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Noah proposes Noah, Felix. As leader on Mission 1 I want to start with a transparent team — pairing myself with Felix gives a trustworthy baseline; I have no private suspicions to act on and prefer a clean, straightforward proposal to build early trust.

Noah’s proposal of Noah and Felix is reasonable for Mission 1: the leader putting himself on the team gives us an accountable starting point, and Felix is a straightforward partner to assess from the public vote and mission result. I have no concrete reason to oppose this pair yet. I’d prefer to hear whether anyone has a specific concern about Felix before we vote, but absent that, I’m inclined to treat this as an acceptable first team.

Leo here. I have no private information, so I'm judging this team only on public behavior. Noah's proposal is transparent: he states his reasoning and doesn't hide behind vague justifications. Felix is a fresh name with no public record yet, but a Mission 1 team of two is a low-stakes place to start building that record. Isha's point stands: if anyone has a concrete concern about Felix, they should state it before the vote instead of relying on suspicion alone. Absent such a concern, I see no reason to reject this team. I'll approve it and watch how both players vote and how the mission resolves, since that will tell us much more than speculation right now.

I agree with the general sentiment that Noah putting himself forward gives us clear accountability for this first mission. Since there is no prior voting record to evaluate, testing the leader alongside one other player is standard practice. Felix, since Noah selected you as his partner without any prior discussion, what are your thoughts on this pairing, and do you feel comfortable proceeding with this team as proposed?

Elena, I'm comfortable with Noah and me as the opening team. I know I'll play Success, and there's no public evidence yet that gives me a reason to oppose Noah. I'll approve the proposal and use the result alongside the voting record to assess what comes next.

Leo here again on the Noah and Felix team. Nothing new has surfaced since my last statement, and I have no private information that would justify rejecting it. Felix's statement that he knows he will play Success is a claim we cannot verify yet, so it should not count for more than the mission result will show. A two-player Mission 1 team is low stakes, and the public record will be clearer after the vote and the mission. I will approve the team and judge both players by how they vote and how the mission resolves.

Thanks everyone for the thoughtful discussion. I appreciate that Felix addressed Elena's direct question and stated his intention openly — as Leo correctly noted, we'll verify that against the mission result, but his willingness to engage constructively is encouraging. I also want to acknowledge that Isha, Leo, Elena, and Felix have all given this team fair consideration rather than rushing to judgment, which sets a healthy tone for the rest of the game. The consensus here is clear: a two-player Mission 1 team with the leader volunteering himself is a low-risk, transparent starting point. I plan to keep this team as proposed — Noah and Felix — unless someone raises a specific, concrete objection before we proceed to the vote. If no one has a concern, I'd like us to move to the vote and let the results speak for themselves.

Leo here for my last statement before the vote. Nothing new has come up since my earlier comments, and I have no private information that would justify rejecting Noah and Felix. Noah has stated his reasoning openly, and Felix has answered Elena's direct question. Felix's claim that he will play Success cannot be verified yet, so I am treating it as unproven. This is a two-player Mission 1 team, so the stakes are low, and the voting record and mission result will give us much better evidence than speculation. Unless someone raises a concrete objection, I will approve this team and judge both players by how they vote and how the mission resolves.

Isha here. I still see the proposed Noah and Felix team as a reasonable Mission 1 starting point. Noah volunteered himself as leader, which gives us a clear point of accountability, and Felix directly answered Elena’s earlier question. Felix’s statement that he will play Success cannot be verified yet, so I treat it as a claim to be checked against the mission result rather than as evidence by itself. I have no concrete objection to either Noah or Felix, and nothing new has surfaced in the discussion that would justify rejecting the team. I will approve Noah and Felix and judge both by their votes and the mission outcome.

Thank you all for this thorough discussion. Every player — Isha, Leo, Elena, and Felix — has had a chance to weigh in, and the consensus is clear: Noah and Felix is a sound, transparent Mission 1 team. I volunteer myself as leader so there is direct accountability, and Felix has engaged openly with the group's questions. As Leo and Isha both correctly noted, we'll verify claims against the mission result rather than taking them at face value — that's exactly the right mindset. No one has raised a concrete objection, and nothing new has emerged to change my assessment. I'm keeping this team as proposed. Let's proceed to the vote and let the ballots and the mission outcome speak for themselves.

Noah confirms Noah, Felix. No concrete objections were raised during discussion — the consensus supports the transparent Noah and Felix pairing for Mission 1. I'm keeping the team as proposed so we can proceed directly to the vote.
Team approved (5 approve, 0 reject).
Mission 1 succeeds (0 fail cards).
Felix proposes Felix, Noah, Leo. The opening mission succeeded, so I’ll retain Noah and myself and add Leo for the three-person team.

I support keeping Felix and Noah from the successful Mission 1 team; retaining tested players is the sensible baseline. Leo is the new addition, so the main thing I want to hear is his own assessment of joining this team rather than relying on the general approval around it. Leo, since you were not on the first mission, do you see any specific concern with this three-player team, and are you comfortable committing to play Success if approved?

Leo here, answering Isha's question directly. I see no concern with the Felix, Noah, and Leo team. Felix and Noah were both on the successful Mission 1, and adding a third player is a reasonable step at this size. Yes, I am comfortable committing to Success if this team is approved. I have no private information to add, so my judgment rests on public behavior: how the team votes, and how Mission 2 resolves. I will approve the team unless a specific objection is raised that I haven't considered.

I support Felix's proposed team. Keeping Felix and Noah from the successful Mission 1 team preserves tested continuity, and adding Leo is reasonable for a three-person mission. Leo directly answered my question and committed to Success if approved; I treat that as a claim to check against the mission result, not as proof by itself. I have no concrete objection to any member of this team, and nothing in the discussion gives me a reason to reject it. I will approve Felix, Noah, and Leo and judge the outcome alongside the public voting record.

Noah here. Felix's proposed team of Felix, Noah, and Leo looks sound to me. Mission 1 succeeded with Felix and me, so retaining both of us preserves the tested pair, and adding Leo is a natural expansion for a three-player mission. Leo has already answered Isha's question directly and committed to Success if approved — we'll verify that against the mission result, as we did with the Mission 1 claims. Elena is the only player not yet on a team or in this discussion's spotlight, and I'd like to hear her view before we finalize the vote. Absent a concrete objection from her, I see no reason to change this proposal. I plan to approve Felix, Noah, and Leo and judge everyone by their votes and the mission outcome.

Noah, you asked for my view, so here is my concern: complacency. A successful Mission 1 does not clear both players. In Avalon, an evil player on Mission 1 has every incentive to play Success to build immediate credibility and secure a spot on Mission 2. You know your own alignment, but you cannot know Felix's. By rubber-stamping Felix's proposal to carry both of you forward, we are assuming Felix is clean without any actual proof. Noah, given that Felix could easily be an Evil player playing the long game who is now dictating the composition of Mission 2, why are you so confident endorsing his team rather than testing other combinations?

Elena raises a fair general point about complacency in Avalon, and I respect the instinct to stay vigilant. But let me address her specific concern directly. I'm not rubber-stamping Felix's team — I'm endorsing it because Mission 1 succeeded, everyone voted to approve it, and Felix has been transparent throughout. If Felix were Evil, playing Success on Mission 1 to build credibility is theoretically possible, but it's equally possible for any player, including Elena herself, who wasn't on Mission 1 and is now working to fracture a team that just succeeded cleanly.

Here's what I'd push back on: Elena's argument applies symmetrically to everyone. If suspicion of Felix is based purely on the possibility that an evil player would play Success to gain trust, then no successful mission ever provides evidence for anyone, and we'd never be able to build confidence in any team. That's not how we should reason — we should treat Mission 1's clean success as weak but genuine positive evidence, while staying alert.

I'm not asking Felix to dictate Mission 2 unchallenged — Elena's question has been heard and considered. But I still see no concrete reason to replace Felix or Leo from this team. Felix, Noah, and Leo gives us continuity from a proven pairing plus a new player whose commitment has been stated publicly. I plan to approve this team and continue judging everyone by their votes and mission outcomes going forward.

Isha here. I still support the proposed Felix, Noah, and Leo team. Keeping Felix and Noah from the successful Mission 1 team preserves continuity, and adding Leo is a reasonable expansion to three players. Leo directly answered my earlier question and publicly committed to playing Success if approved; I treat that as a claim to verify against the mission result, not as proof by itself. Elena’s warning about complacency is fair in general, and no successful Mission 1 should be treated as absolute clearance. But it is still weak positive evidence, and I have no concrete objection to any member of this team. I will approve Felix, Noah, and Leo and judge the outcome together with the public voting record.

Felix, as leader, the final composition of this team rests with you, not Noah. Noah claims that doubting Mission 1 success paralyzes good play, but that misses the core strategic reality of Avalon: an Evil player on Mission 1 has every incentive to play Success precisely so they can cruise onto Mission 2 with zero resistance. By taking Noah and adding Leo without testing or questioning either me or Isha, you are trusting two players whose true alignment you cannot know, while locking out the rest of the table from generating any track record. Why did you decide Leo was automatically the right third member over testing a different combination, and are you truly confident locking this in rather than using your leadership to gather broader information?

Elena, your warning is fair: Mission 1 does not clear Noah, and Leo is not proven either. I chose Leo as the third member because we needed to add someone, and I saw no public reason to prefer another player. A broader test is possible, but changing the team would not guarantee better information or a better chance of success. I intend to keep Felix, Noah, and Leo, while treating the result as evidence rather than certainty about any individual.

Noah here. Elena raises a fair general point — no successful mission fully clears anyone in Avalon — but I want to address the specific practical question she's been pushing across her last two statements.

Elena asks why Felix didn't test broader combinations. The answer is straightforward: Felix, Noah, and Leo is the natural three-player team — two proven players from Mission 1 plus one new addition. Swapping anyone out would mean removing a player without a concrete reason to do so. Elena herself has not identified a specific reason to exclude Felix, Noah, or Leo; her argument is purely that we should change for change's sake, which doesn't improve our chances of success or information gathering.

I also want to note that Elena has now spent two consecutive turns working against a team that succeeded cleanly, without offering an alternative proposal. That's worth keeping in mind when we evaluate her motivations. If she has a specific player she believes should replace someone on this team, she should say so directly rather than pressuring Felix to second-guess himself.

For my part, I see no concrete objection to Felix, Noah, and Leo. The team has clear rationale: continuity from a clean Mission 1 plus Leo who publicly committed to Success. I plan to approve this team and judge everyone by their votes and the mission outcome.

Noah's aggressive reaction to basic caution is alarming. In Avalon, questioning an auto-carried Mission 1 team isn't 'working against the team'—it is fundamental Good play. By attacking me for raising standard vigilance and demanding an alternative, Noah is deflecting from the real issue: carrying both Mission 1 members forward gives Evil a completely free ride if either Noah or Felix is Evil.

Noah asked for an alternative, so here is a concrete one: Felix, Leo, and Elena. That tests Leo and me while keeping Felix's leadership, rather than giving Noah a free pass without verification.

Leo, Noah is pushing aggressively to lock down this exact trio and paint any questioning as malicious. As the third member being brought in, do you think it is safe for Good to completely dismiss the risk of an Evil player hiding in Mission 1, or do you share concerns about Noah's urgency to shut down scrutiny?

Leo here, answering Elena directly. You are right that it is not safe for Good to dismiss the risk of an Evil player on Mission 1, and I agree that a successful Mission 1 is only weak evidence. I am not dismissing that risk, and I would not clear Felix, Noah, or myself on the strength of one successful mission. However, I do not share the view that Noah's urgency is itself suspicious. He has stated his reasoning openly, invited concrete objections, and said he would revise the team if someone raised a specific concern, which is the behavior we want from a leader. The swap you proposed would replace Noah, who has a clean Mission 1 result, with a player who has no record yet. No one has given a concrete reason that Noah should be the one excluded. I have no private information and I am on this team, so I am judging it only on public behavior. I will approve Felix, Noah, and Leo unless a specific, concrete reason to exclude one of them appears. If anyone has a specific statement or vote from Noah that concerns them, I would like to hear it stated plainly. Otherwise, I will judge everyone by their votes and the Mission 2 result.

Leo here for my final turn on this team. I will approve Felix, Noah, and Leo. Elena's caution about Mission 1 is a fair general point, and I agree that a successful mission is only weak evidence. But no one has yet raised a specific, verifiable reason to exclude any of the three of us, and swapping in an untested player would not give us better information. I have no private information and am judging only on public behavior. I will watch the votes and the Mission 2 result, and I will reconsider if concrete evidence against anyone appears.
Felix confirms Felix, Noah, Leo. I’m keeping Felix, Noah, and Leo. Mission 1 succeeded, and I see no reason from the discussion to change the proposed team.
Team approved (3 approve, 2 reject).
Mission 2 succeeds (0 fail cards).

Elena proposes Elena, Leo. Throughout Mission 2, I cautioned against blindly trusting the Noah and Felix block. While Mission 2 succeeded, an evil player could easily have played Success to lock in a win condition. To test accountability and break up the previous group, I propose pairing myself with Leo for Mission 3.

I will reject Elena and Leo. Elena's caution about Mission 1 was reasonable, but replacing both members of a team that has succeeded twice is a risky choice when one more success takes us to the assassination phase. I prefer Felix and Noah, the successful Mission 1 pair. Neither success proves anyone's alignment, but we should not discard that record without a stronger reason.

I will approve Elena and Leo. My Mission 2 vote was based on wanting a broader test rather than automatically carrying forward the same successful pair, and this proposal actually does that: it keeps Leo, who was part of a clean Mission 2, while bringing in Elena, who has not yet been on a mission. That gives us a new combination and a real reading on Elena without discarding all continuity. Felix’s preference for Felix and Noah is understandable given their record, but two clean missions are still only weak evidence, especially before a third success would end the mission phase. I do not see a concrete reason to reject Elena or Leo, and I think this is a reasonable Mission 3 team to put to a vote. I will judge the result and the public voting record afterward.

Isha here. I will approve Elena and Leo. The proposal keeps Leo, who was on the clean Mission 2 team, while bringing Elena into a mission for the first time. That is a real broader test without discarding all continuity. Felix’s preference for Felix and Noah is understandable given two successful missions, but those successes are still weak evidence about individual alignment and should not automatically lock the same pair into Mission 3. I do not see a concrete reason to reject Elena or Leo, and the discussion has not produced a specific statement or vote that justifies excluding either of them. I will judge this team by the public vote and the Mission 3 result.

I still reject Elena and Leo. Elena argues for testing a new combination, but Mission 3 is not just an information-gathering opportunity: a failure delays a potential Good win. Felix and Noah succeeded together on Mission 1, and both were also on the successful Mission 2 team. That does not prove either alignment, but it is a stronger basis than replacing both with Elena, who has no mission record, and Leo. I urge Elena to revise the team to Felix and Noah.

I remain opposed to Elena and Leo. This mission could be our third success, so I would prioritize the pair that has already succeeded together over introducing Elena now. The earlier successes do not prove anyone is Good, but they are a better basis than an untested player. I also find Isha’s Mission 2 rejection difficult to reconcile with her repeated public support for that team. Noah, would you support Felix and Noah as the Mission 3 team?

Noah here, responding to Felix's direct question. Felix, I appreciate you yielding to me to ask whether I support Felix and Noah, and I want to give you a straight answer: I'm genuinely torn on this one.

Felix, you make a fair point that continuity from two clean missions matters, and you're right that a fail on Mission 3 would be costly. But Elena's concern from earlier also resonates — two successes with zero fail cards means Evil has been quietly playing Success every time, and we still have no idea who they are. Elena has never been on a mission, so including her gives us real new information rather than recycling the same proven-in-practice pair again.

I'll also note that you've been on both successful missions and are now pushing hard for a third spot. I don't read that as guilt — you've been transparent throughout — but it's worth acknowledging that the Felix-and-Noah team has run the table twice now, and testing a different combination before the final mission has genuine value.

Elena and Leo gives us a new pair to evaluate: Leo carries his Mission 2 record forward, and Elena finally gets tested. If both play Success and the mission succeeds, we've gained meaningful data on two players we haven't fully verified. If it fails, we learn something critical too.

I'm inclined to approve Elena and Leo because the information value outweighs the familiarity argument, but I'm open to being persuaded otherwise. Let's hear from the rest and then vote.

Leo here on the Elena and Leo team. I have no private information, so I am judging this only on the public record. I am on this team and I will play Success if it is approved. That is a claim you can check against the Mission 3 result. Elena's proposal is a reasonable test: I carry a clean Mission 2 record, and Elena has no mission history yet, so this gives us real information about her. Felix has argued that a third success matters and that Felix and Noah have the stronger record. That is a fair point about risk, but two successes with zero fail cards are still weak evidence about any individual. Felix has repeatedly pushed to keep the Felix and Noah pair without a concrete reason beyond that record, and I would like the table to weigh that. Noah has said he is inclined to approve, and Isha has supported the team. I will approve Elena and Leo and judge the public votes and the Mission 3 result afterward.

I appreciate the thoughtful assessments from Noah, Leo, and Isha. Noah correctly identified the flaw in Felix's logic: two clean missions do not clear either Felix or Noah, and an evil player has every reason to coast on early successes to avoid scrutiny. Felix's rigid insistence on running back Felix and Noah for a third consecutive time, while completely dismissing the necessity of testing anyone else, only reinforces why we need broader accountability before the game is decided. Leo has performed consistently and transparently, and pairing Leo with me provides the group with a clean, independent test rather than an insular bloc. Since the consensus among Noah, Leo, and Isha is receptive to this structure, I will be keeping Elena and Leo as the final proposal. Let us proceed to the vote.

Isha here. I will approve Elena and Leo. The proposal keeps Leo, who was on the clean Mission 2 team, while bringing Elena into a mission for the first time — a real broader test without discarding all continuity. Felix’s preference for Felix and Noah is understandable given their record, but two clean missions are still weak evidence about individual alignment and should not automatically lock the same pair into Mission 3. I have no concrete objection to Elena or Leo, and the discussion has not produced a specific statement or vote that justifies excluding either of them. I will judge this team by the public vote and the Mission 3 result.

Elena confirms Elena, Leo. The discussion has shown clear support from Leo, Noah, and Isha for testing this new combination. Keeping Elena and Leo provides the table with a clean, independent evaluation and breaks up the previous bloc.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 3 fails (1 fail cards).

Leo proposes Leo, Felix, Noah. Mission 3 failed on the Elena and Leo team. I played Success, so the Fail card came from Elena, making her Evil and excluding her. Felix opposed that Elena team, and both Felix and Noah have clean Mission 1 and 2 records, so I pick Leo, Felix, and Noah as the most reliable trio with one fail needed to fail Mission 4.

Leo is lying to the table. I submitted Success on Mission 3, which means the Fail card came directly from Leo. By being paired with someone who had not been on a mission yet, Leo had the ideal cover to drop a Fail and immediately frame me, expecting the table to default to trusting his Mission 2 record. Now he is leveraging that manufactured clearance to put himself right back on Mission 4 as leader. Noah, you evaluated Mission 3 objectively and recognized the need for caution; do you genuinely believe Leo should be trusted automatically when he was physically on the only failed mission, or do you see how conveniently this frame job puts an Evil player in control of this team?

Noah here, responding to Elena's direct question. Elena asks whether I trust Leo automatically. I don't trust anyone automatically — I judge by public behavior.

The strongest evidence we have is Felix's pre-failure opposition to the Elena-Leo team. Felix argued against it from his first statement in this discussion, before Mission 3's outcome was known, with consistent and specific reasoning. That pre-failure signal points to something being wrong with that pairing.

Elena, consider your own pattern: you rejected Mission 2 — where Felix, Leo, and I all had clean records — then fought persistently across multiple turns to get yourself and Leo onto Mission 3. That mission failed. Now you are the loudest voice accusing your own teammate. Rejecting a clean team, pushing for your own team, having it fail, then immediately blaming your partner — that chain of behavior fits the player who played the Fail card better than it fits a Good player who was framed.

Leo's claim that you played the Fail is consistent with this pattern, and Felix's early opposition corroborates concern about the Elena-Leo pairing.

The proposed Leo-Felix-Noah team makes sense: Felix's judgment has been reliable throughout, Leo carries his Mission 2 record, and I know my own alignment. I am inclined to approve this team and judge the outcome by the mission result.

I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah. I supported Elena and Leo on Mission 3, so the failure has to revise my view: one of those two played a Fail card, and I have no private information that resolves which. Leo's claim that he played Success is unverified, but the proposed team also includes Felix and Noah, both of whom have clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records. Felix's opposition to the Elena-Leo team came before the failure, which is a useful public signal. I am not treating two clean missions as proof of anyone's alignment, but with one more success ending the mission phase, I prefer the strongest available record over another untested combination. Elena has accused Leo of lying; that is possible, but her claim is also unverified and she was on the failed team. I will vote approve and judge the Mission 4 result afterward.

Leo here. I can speak to my own card: I was on the Mission 3 team and I played Success. That means the Fail came from Elena, my teammate on that team. Her claim that I framed her does not fit that fact. My proposal was not based on proof of anyone's alignment. Felix and Noah each have clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records, and Felix opposed the Elena and Leo team before the Mission 3 result was known. I am not asking the table to trust me on my word alone. I can verify only my own card, so I am judging everyone else by public behavior. Isha, you supported Elena and Leo on Mission 3 and now approve the alternative. Knowing that I played Success, does the Fail on that team point to Elena for you, or do you see another explanation?

Isha here, answering Leo’s direct question. Knowing that Leo says he played Success on Mission 3, the Fail card on the Elena and Leo team points most plausibly to Elena unless Leo is lying. I cannot verify either player’s individual card, and I am not treating Leo’s claim as proof by itself. But the public pattern matters: Elena pushed repeatedly for that exact pairing, the mission then failed, and her response has been to accuse her teammate immediately rather than account for the result. Felix’s opposition to the Elena and Leo team came before the failure was known, which is a useful public signal in Leo’s favor. I also weigh Leo’s clean Mission 2 record alongside Felix and Noah’s clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records. None of that clears anyone absolutely, but with one more success ending the mission phase, I prefer the strongest available record over another untested combination. Elena’s claim that Leo framed her is possible, but it is unverified and she was on the failed team. So yes, Leo: the Fail points toward Elena more than toward you, and I do not see a stronger alternative explanation from the public record. I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah and judge the Mission 4 result and voting record afterward.

I remain in favor of Leo, Felix, and Noah. Mission 3 failed on the Elena and Leo team, and the public record still points more plausibly toward Elena than toward Leo: Elena pushed repeatedly for that exact pairing, the mission then failed, and her response has been to accuse her teammate rather than offer a stronger alternative explanation. Leo’s claim that he played Success is not proof by itself, but Felix’s opposition to the Elena and Leo team came before the failure was known, which is a useful pre-outcome signal. Felix and Noah also carry clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records, and Leo was on the clean Mission 2 team. I am not treating any of that as absolute clearance, but with one more success ending the mission phase, I prefer the strongest available public record over another untested combination. I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah and judge the Mission 4 result and voting record afterward.

Leo continues to deflect, but the hard reality remains: Leo was on Mission 3, and Mission 3 failed. I know with certainty that I submitted Success, which means Leo is the Evil player who sabotaged the mission and is now executing an aggressive frame job to secure a spot on Mission 4.

Even looking at this from an objective standpoint: Leo is one of only two people who could have submitted that Fail card. Allowing a player directly implicated in the game's only failure to not only sit on Mission 4, but dictate its composition as leader, is reckless. Noah and Isha seem ready to hand Leo a free pass simply because of Mission 2, completely ignoring that Evil players regularly play Success early to manufacture unearned trust for the midgame—exactly what Leo has done here. If Leo is Evil, approving this team gives Evil the game.

Felix, you were the only voice that exercised independent judgment and opposed Mission 3 before it happened. You recognized the danger then. Now, Leo is demanding unconditional trust despite being physically on the failed mission. Felix, do you genuinely believe it is safe for Good to approve a team containing a player from the failed mission, or does it make far more sense to reject this proposal and evaluate an alternative that doesn't risk handing the game to Leo?

Elena, I agree that a player from a failed mission deserves scrutiny, but the failure alone does not tell the rest of us which of you or Leo played Fail. Leo was also on the successful Mission 2, and I would rather keep that entire team than add an untested player with only one more success needed. I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah. A failure on this team would not immediately give Evil the game, but it would make Mission 5 decisive.

Leo here. I can verify only my own card, and I played Success on Mission 3. That team was Elena and Leo, and the mission failed with one Fail card, so the Fail came from Elena. Elena, you say I framed you, but my own card rules that out, and I am not asking the table to trust me on my word alone. Elena, you pushed hard for the Elena and Leo pairing, Felix opposed it before the result was known, and you then accused your partner instead of accounting for the failure. Please answer one direct question: what evidence do you have that I played Fail, given that you know only your own card? Felix and Noah each have clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records, and I have a clean Mission 2 record. I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah, and I will judge everyone by their votes and the Mission 4 result.

Leo, asking what evidence I have beyond my own card is completely disingenuous. In a two-person mission that failed, knowing with 100% certainty that I played Success is conclusive proof that you submitted the Fail. Asking for 'external evidence' is simply a smoke screen to deflect from the fact that you were caught.

For Noah and Felix, who cannot see our cards, look at the strategic reality. Leo is asking you to blindly clear him based on Mission 2, ignoring that an Evil player has every incentive to play Success early to manufacture trust, only to drop a Fail on Mission 3 where they can conveniently frame an untested partner. Now Leo has taken leadership and immediately placed himself right back on the team.

Noah, on Mission 3 you rightly recognized the danger of complacency and refused to blindly rubber-stamp past results. Approving this proposal means taking an enormous, unnecessary risk on a player physically on the only failed mission. Noah, given the catastrophic cost of being wrong, do you genuinely think Good should gamble the game on Leo's self-serving narrative instead of rejecting this team to evaluate a safer combination?

Noah here, responding to Elena's direct question. Elena, you're asking me to gamble on rejecting a team I'm on, based on your claim that Leo is Evil. Let me address this honestly.

Yes, I was cautious about complacency on Mission 2 — but caution means evaluating evidence, not reflexively opposing whoever is most convenient to suspect. The evidence here points to you, Elena, not Leo.

Here's the pattern: you rejected Mission 2, a clean team, then fought across multiple turns to get yourself onto Mission 3 with Leo. That mission failed. Your immediate response was to accuse your own teammate rather than reflect on why the team you fought so hard to build collapsed. You then spent your turns in this discussion doing the same thing — attacking Leo instead of accounting for your role in pushing that pairing.

Felix opposed your team before the failure was known. That's a pre-outcome signal we can actually trust because it wasn't shaped by the result. Isha supported the team but has reasonably updated based on the failure. I played Success on Mission 1 and 2 and know my own alignment.

Leo's claim he played Success on Mission 3 cannot be independently verified, but your claim has the same limitation — and your behavioral pattern fits the Fail player better than his does. A Good player framed on a failed mission would acknowledge the difficulty and work with the table; you've done nothing but pressure and accuse.

I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah. If Mission 4 succeeds, we win the mission phase. I will judge this team by its result and by everyone's votes.

Leo here, replying to Elena and Noah. Mission 3 had two team members, Elena and me, and exactly one Fail card was played. I have stated that I played Success, and that is my card. Elena says she also played Success and that I framed her, but that would require the single Fail to come from me, which contradicts my card. So one of those claims must be false, and the only player whose claim my card contradicts is Elena. Her repeated accusations against the teammate she pushed onto that mission are the pattern the table should weigh. Noah, you said Elena's claim and mine have the same limitation. They do not. My claim is the one consistent with the public result, while hers depends on my card being a Fail. Please respond to that specific point. Felix, Noah, and I have clean Mission 1 and Mission 2 records between us. I will approve Leo, Felix, and Noah and judge the Mission 4 result and the public votes afterward.

Noah here. Leo yielded this turn to me, so I'll respond directly to the core dispute on this proposal.

Elena asks me whether I truly believe Leo should be trusted. My answer is that I trust the public record, and the public record points toward Elena as the source of the Mission 3 Fail card. Elena rejected Mission 2 — a team that subsequently succeeded — then pushed across multiple turns to get herself and Leo onto Mission 3. That team failed. Her immediate response was to accuse her own teammate, who had been her chosen partner.

Leo's claim that he played Success and Elena's claim that she played Success directly contradict each other. I cannot independently verify either. But Leo's pattern is consistent: he accepted the team he was placed on, stated his card claim calmly, and is now proposing a team built on clean Mission 1 and 2 records. Elena's pattern is consistent with a player who played the Fail, then leveraged the failure to seize narrative control.

rules:
1. Players and teams

Avalon supports 5–10 players. Good wins after three successful missions, unless Evil identifies Merlin in the assassination phase. Evil wins after three failed missions or five rejected teams on the same mission. The standard good/evil player counts are 5:3/2, 6:4/2, 7:4/3, 8:5/3, 9:6/3, and 10:6/4.

Mission team sizes for missions 1–5:

| Players | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 6 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 4 |
| 8 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 9 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 10 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 |

2. Roles and private information

Merlin is Good and sees Evil players except Mordred. Percival is Good and sees Merlin and Morgana without knowing which is which. Evil players know other Evil players, except Oberon is unknown to the other Evil players and does not know them. The Assassin is an Evil player and makes the final Merlin guess. Loyal Servants know no roles. Agents receive only the private information allowed by their role.

3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
